title: Seahawks Set to Welcome Sam Darnold Back to Practice Wednesday, ESPN Reports
body:
Seattle’s quarterback room gets a boost on Wednesday as Sam Darnold is slated to re‑join the Seahawks’ practice squad after missing the first two contests with a glute strain. Head coach Mike Macdonald hinted that the former New York Jets and Carolina Panthers signal‑caller could be cleared to suit up for the team’s upcoming matchup in Washington, adding a “chance” that the veteran will see game action this week.

The return comes at a pivotal moment for a Seahawks offense that has struggled to find rhythm without its starter. Darnold, who was acquired in a trade with the Carolina Panthers earlier this season, has been limited to a handful of snaps in preseason and has yet to log a regular‑season snap. His absence forced Seattle to rely on backup quarterbacks who have been unable to generate consistent drives, leaving the team winless after two games and trailing the NFC West leader by a considerable margin. The glute injury, diagnosed as a Grade 2 strain, sidelined Darnold for approximately three weeks, but the medical staff reports that he has progressed well in rehab and is expected to participate fully in the Wednesday walkthrough.

Macdonald’s comments reflect a broader strategic shift. Since taking over as defensive coordinator last season, the former Baltimore Ravens assistant has been tasked with revamping Seattle’s offensive approach, emphasizing quicker releases and more mobility from the pocket. Darnold’s skill set—particularly his ability to extend plays with his legs and deliver accurate throws on the run—aligns with the new scheme. If the quarterback can regain full health, he could provide the spark needed to diversify the playbook, which has leaned heavily on short passes and a run‑first mentality under current offensive coordinator Shane Waldron.

Analysts note that Darnold’s potential return also carries implications for the team’s long‑term quarterback planning. Seattle entered the 2024 season with a clear intention to develop a younger talent at the position, but injuries to both the starter and key backups have forced the organization to lean on a veteran with a mixed track record. Darnold, who posted a 3‑8 record with the Jets and a 4‑13 finish in Carolina, has shown flashes of brilliance when healthy, posting a 92.5 passer rating in the 2023 season with the Panthers. A successful comeback could buy the Seahawks valuable time to evaluate their developmental prospects without the pressure of immediate results.

The upcoming contest against Washington presents a low‑stakes environment for Darnold to earn his first regular‑season snap. The Commanders, also navigating a rebuilding year, have struggled defensively against mobile quarterbacks, ranking near the bottom of the league in sacks and pressures allowed. This matchup could serve as a low‑pressure testing ground for Seattle’s revamped offensive concepts, allowing Macdonald and Waldron to gauge Darnold’s chemistry with his receivers and his comfort in the new system.

Looking ahead, the Seahawks’ trajectory hinges on how quickly Darnold can re‑establish his rhythm and whether the coaching staff can integrate his mobility into a cohesive attack. If he remains healthy and productive, Seattle could pivot from a tentative start to a competitive mid‑season contender, easing the pressure on its younger roster pieces. Conversely, lingering doubts about his durability could prompt the franchise to double down on its long‑term quarterback development plan. For now, the practice field in Scottsdale will be the first stage where Darnold seeks to rewrite his narrative and help the Seahawks revive a faltering season.
